summary: Annual reviews, ongoing service, suitability concerns and benefit calculations. My experience with pension complaints informs the evidence and review pathways.
evidence: Review invitations, completion records and communications
Relevant fact-find, objectives and suitability report
control: Separate a missed service review from a finding of unsuitable advice. Route suitability and loss questions to an authorised specialist.

summary: Instruction delays, disclosures, calculations and suitability concerns across a fictional investment case population.
control: Confirm the instruction timeline and agreed service. Suitability and investment-loss assessment require specialist review.

summary: Interest disputes, calculation errors and communication failures, with the same governed complaint controls.
evidence: Account terms and applicable rate history
control: Reconcile the rate, period and calculation evidence before determining the outcome or remedy.

summary: Payment allocation, servicing complaints and investigation delays across a fictional mortgage population.
control: Reconcile payments and servicing events. Refer complex financial-impact or support questions to the appropriate reviewer.

summary: Arrears-related complaints, affordability concerns, forbearance and repayment-arrangement reviews. Collections is an operational context, not a separate financial product.
control: Assess the complaint and support needs with an authorised reviewer. No automated collection action, affordability decision or arrangement approval.

summary: Two distinct pathways: commission/disclosure complaints and vehicle quality, repairs and warranty disputes. Case oversight does not determine regulatory eligibility or mechanical liability.
evidence: Commission and disclosure evidence, where relevant
Vehicle age, mileage, fault chronology and inspection evidence
Repair history, warranty wording and disputed parts/modifications
control: Keep commission and vehicle-quality pathways distinct. Technical safety, warranty, liability and any scheme-specific decisions require qualified human assessment.
